topicCandidates: Foreign and domestic-source income, non-permanent-resident remittances, treaty relief, foreign tax credits, and the records required to support cross-border positions.
Side-work income classification, necessary expenses, bookkeeping, business commencement, blue-return applications, and the separation of tax treatment from immigration and employment permission.
Consumption-tax taxable-person tests, base and specified periods, voluntary elections, qualified-invoice registration, public registration data, filing duties, and cancellation consequences.
Departure-year national income tax, quasi-final returns, national and local tax agents, resident-tax bills after departure, continuing Japanese-source income, and secure notice handling.
userSituations: A resident receives overseas salary, rent, investments, pension, or freelance payments and assumes the foreign payer or bank account keeps the income outside Japan.
A person pays tax abroad and assumes Japan automatically removes all double taxation without a treaty procedure or foreign-tax-credit filing.
An employee starts freelance work and assumes a tax registration or final return also grants immigration or employer permission.
A freelancer labels every cost as an expense or assumes every recurring side activity is automatically business income.
A small supplier registers to issue qualified invoices at a client's request without understanding the consumption-tax filing, publication, recordkeeping, and cancellation consequences.
A resident leaves Japan before annual filing or a later resident-tax notice and assumes municipal deregistration ends the tax obligations.
edgeCasesAndExceptions: Income source is a legal classification and does not necessarily follow payer, currency, contract, or account location.

Tax treaties differ by jurisdiction, income type, residence, beneficial ownership, duration, payer, permanent establishment, and procedural requirements; a 183-day phrase is not a universal exemption.
Foreign tax credit is limited, evidence-based, and can require continuous carryover statements; foreign tax charged above a treaty limit may not be creditable.
Business income and miscellaneous income are determined from the activity's facts and records, not a preferred label; loss and bookkeeping consequences differ.
A tax-exempt business can become a consumption-tax filer through a taxable-person election or qualified-invoice registration even below the ordinary base-period threshold.
Qualified-invoice registration publishes defined sole-proprietor information and can continue taxable-person consequences after cancellation.
Leaving Japan without appointing a national tax agent can require a quasi-final return and payment before departure; resident tax uses a separate local process and agent appointment.
Japanese-source income or business matters can continue after departure.
jurisdictionVariables: Tax residence, income source and category, earning and payment location, remittances, foreign tax, treaty jurisdiction, and required applications or certificates.
Continuity, scale, profit purpose, records, business organization, client relationship, expenses, assets, employees, and municipal or prefectural business-tax requirements.
Taxable sales in the base and specified periods, payroll alternative, elections, invoice registration date, taxable purchases, simplified treatment, and cancellation timing.
Departure date, loss of domicile or residence, filing requirement, agent appointment, January 1 municipality, collection method, continuing income, business closure, and refund timing.

contentImpacts.reason: Provide a safe cross-border decision path without reducing treaty or credit rules to slogans.
Separate income-tax classification and records from the existing immigration-focused side-work guide.
Explain a separate tax that can be triggered by sales, elections, or invoice registration.
Coordinate national and local departure obligations without overloading the general departure checklist.
Link the focused international, independent-work, consumption-tax, and departure guides.
Add conditional cross-border, independent-work, and departure tax branches.
Route common foreign-payer and foreign-account assumptions to sourced guidance.

scopeBoundaries: The guides teach issue spotting and records, not treaty interpretation, foreign-tax-credit calculations, income classification verdicts, expense approval, or consumption-tax calculations.
Corporate tax, inheritance and gift tax, securities exit tax, customs, and detailed prefectural enterprise tax remain outside this pass except for warnings to seek appropriate advice.
Tax filings and business notices do not grant immigration permission, employer consent, a professional license, or municipal operating permission.
Municipal resident-tax departure procedures are described as locally verified steps rather than one national form.
Annual thresholds, relief measures, forms, and treaty lists require current-source confirmation.
